cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet in Judah, has been carrying the LORD's hard words to Judah's kings (Jeremiah 22:1-2). One of them, Coniah, just heard that none of his descendants will rule again in Judah (Jeremiah 22:30). Now the LORD declares woe on the shepherds.

cards.question: Shepherds are supposed to look after sheep. What does the LORD say these shepherds are doing to the sheep instead?
The LORD calls these sheep the shepherds' own flock.

cards.text: The LORD says it plain: they scattered His flock, drove them away and didn't attend to them. Friend, that's like me spending all morning packing cookie boxes and then FLINGING them out the back door into the street.

cards.question: The shepherds didn't attend to the LORD's flock. So who does the LORD say He'll attend to for the evil of their deeds?

cards.text: They skipped attending, and now THEY get attended to. That is not the kind of attention you want, but the LORD has a plan for the remnant of His flock, scattered across the lands.

cards.question: Somebody has to go get the remnant of the LORD's flock. Who does the LORD say will gather them?
Once He gathers the remnant of His flock, the LORD says He'll return them to their pasture.

cards.text: Back in their pasture, the flock will be fruitful and multiply, and friend, the only thing that ever multiplied in my junk drawer was the dust. Then the LORD takes care of the shepherd problem.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He'll raise up over His gathered flock?
Under the new shepherds, the LORD says a few of His sheep will still go missing.

cards.text: No more fear, no more dismay, and not ONE sheep missing, friend, and I can't even keep track of one oven timer. Then the LORD looks ahead and says the days are coming.

cards.question: Looking ahead, the LORD says He will raise up a righteous Branch for ___.
What does the LORD say this righteous Branch will do?

cards.text: And He will administer justice and righteousness in the land. Those old shepherds couldn't keep a flock together in ONE field, and this King brings justice to the WHOLE land.

cards.question: In the Branch's days, Judah will be ___ and Israel will dwell ___.
The LORD gives the righteous Branch a name. What will He be called?

cards.text: Then the LORD says the days are coming when people will stop saying, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt." Something's coming so big it bumps THAT off the top of the playlist.

cards.question: So when people say "As surely as the LORD lives," what rescue will they name instead of Egypt?

answers.text: Bringing them back from the north

cards.text: From the land of the north and every land He banished them to, the LORD leads them up, and they dwell once more in their own land. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me: "once more in their own land" is the best line in the whole thing.

findings.problem: The setup only says that the days are coming, so nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out that the Branch is for David. This fill-in-the-blank asks for unseen wording rather than a meaning the baker can infer.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: David is a new person in the walkthrough, but he appears only as a bare name in the answer choices and is never simply identified, such as David, Israel's king.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
